newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end lower in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end lower in dull trade.

text.p: China's A and B shares ended down in slow trade on Thursday amid worries that Beijing might enact new anti-speculation policies, brokers said.

The issue of two new B shares in Shanghai sucked a large amount of capital from the secondary market, with institutional investors putting their money into these comparatively cheap new counters, they said.
Jinan Qingqi Motorcycle issued 230 million B shares late in May and Heilongjiang Electric Power offered an additional 80 million shares on Wednesday.
The Shanghai B index fell 0.870 points, or 0.97 percent, to 89.206 on volume of 13.44 million shares worth $9.353 million.
The Shenzhen B share index slid 2.04 points, or 1.28 percent, to end at 156.77 on turnover of HK$48 million against Wednesday's HK$75 million.
Shenzhen's A share index slumped 1.67 points, or 0.35 percent, to 472.50 as turnover contracted to 7.3 billion yuan from eight billion yuan the previous session.
"Investors are apprehensive about widespread talk that there will be some new crackdown measures from Beijing in the near future," said a trader at Shenzhen J&A Securities.
Beijing last month announced a series of policies aimed at reducing speculation in the country's overheated stock markets, sending share prices sharply lower.

"People believe Beijing will sooner or later come out with some bad news for the markets but they do not know how severe the policies will be this time, so they are holding back from large-scale trading," an analyst with China Guotai Securities said.
Brokers said they expected bearish sentiment to continue on Friday, with uncertainties increasing ahead of the weekend when new policies are typically announced.
On the Shenzhen B share market, Shenzhen Properties was the worst performer, shedding HK$0.15, or 4.69 percent, to HK$3.05.
Nanjing Posts and Telecommunication rallied HK$0.02 to HK$4.20 on volume of 2.4 million shares, making it the most actively traded issue.
Shanghai Steel Tube Co was the biggest loser on the Shanghai B share market on speculative selling, slipping $0.014, or 8.53 percent, to $0.150 on volume of 54,000 shares.

Pudong real estate counter Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development was the most actively traded on profit-taking, slipping $0.018, or 2.19 percent, to $0.802 on volume of 1.3 million shares.
The Shanghai A index edged down 0.639 points, or 0.04 percent, at 1,421.435 points on volume of 566.5 million shares worth 9.1 billion yuan.
But the SSE30 blue chip index bucked the market trend on institutional support, rising 13.475 points, or 0.32 percent, to 4,229.539 points.
